questions.q: Consider the function $f: \left(0, \infty\right) \to R$ defined by $f\left(x\right) = e^{- \left|\log_{\mathrm{e}}x\right|}$. If $m$ and $n$ be respectively the number of points at which $f$ is not continuous and $f$ is not differentiable, then $m + n$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We know that, \left|\log x\right|$ is continuous in \left(0, \infty\right)$.

$⇒ f \left(x\right) = e^{- \log \left|x\right|}$ is continuous in \left($0, $\infty\right)

Thus, the number of points where $f \left(x\right)$ is discontinuous is $0$.

$⇒ m = 0$

$f\left(x\right) = \left\{$\begin{cases}e^{\log x}, & 0 < x < 1 \\ e^{- \log x}, & x ≥ 1\end{cases}$\right$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \left\{$\begin{cases}x, & 0 < x < 1 \\ \dfrac{1}{x},& x ≥ 1\end{cases}$\right$

$⇒ f^{'}\left(x\right) = \left\{$\begin{cases}1, & 0 < x < 1 \\ \dfrac{- 1}{x2},& x ≥ 1\end{cases}$\right$

$⇒ f^{'}\left({1}^{-}\right) =1 & f^{'} \left({1}^{+}\right) = -1$

So, the number of points where $f\left(x\right)$ is non-differentiable is $1$.

$⇒ n = 1$

$⇒ m + n = 1

$

Let $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$~be defined as~$f\left(x\right) = \left[\begin{cases}\left[e^{x}\right], & x < 0 \\ ae^{x} + \left[x - 1\right], & 0 \le x < 1 \\ b + \left[sin \left(\pix\right)\right],$ \text{ and } 1 ≤ x < 2 \\ \left[e^{- x}\right] - c, \text{ and } x \ge 2\end{cases}\right$
where $a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}$~and \left[t\right]$~denotes greatest integer less than or equal to $t$. Then, which of the following statements is true?
options: There exists $a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}$~such that~$f$ is continuous of $\mathbb{R}$.
If $f$~is discontinuous at exactly one point, then~$a + b + c = 1$
If $f$~is discontinuous at exactly one point, then $a + b + c \ne 1$.
$f$~is discontinuous at atleast two points, for any values of $a, b$~and $c$.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& $f\left(x\right) = \left[$\begin{cases}\left[e^{x}\right], & x < 0 \\ ae^{x} + \left[x - 1\right], & 0 \le x < 1 \\ b + \left[\sin \left(\pix\right)\right], \text{ and } 1 ≤ x < 2 \\ \left[e^{- x}\right] - c, \text{ and } x \ge 2\end{cases}$\right$

i.e.~$f\left(x\right) = \left\{$\begin{cases}0, & x < 0 \\ ae^{x} - 1, & 0 \le x < 1 \\ b, & x = 1 \\ b - 1, & 1 < x < 2 \\ - c, & x \ge 2\end{cases}$\right$

Here, we know~$f \left(x\right)$~is discontinuous at~$x = 1$~as~$b \ne b - 1$

For $f \left(x\right)$~to be continuous at~$x = 0; a = 1$

For~$f \left(x\right)$~to be continuous at~$x = 2; b + c = 1$

Hence,~$a + b + c = 2$

questions.q: Let $f\left(x\right) = 15 – \left|x – 10\right|; x \in \mathbb{R} .$ Then the set of all values of $x$, at which the function $g\left(x\right) = f ( f\left(x\right) )$ is not differentiable, is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$f \left(x\right) = 15 - \left|$x - 10\right|$

$⇒ $g\left($x\right) = $f\lleft(f\left(x\right))$

$⇒ g\left(x\right) = 15 - \left|f\left(x\right) - 10\right|$

$= 15 - \left|15 - \left|x - 10\right| - 10\right|$

$= 15 - \left|5 - \left|x - 10\right|\right|$

$= 15 - \left|\left|x - 10\right| - 5\right|$

We know that,~\left|x\right| = \left\${$\begin{cases}x, & x ≥ 0 \\ - x, & x < 0\end{cases}$\right$

Case~$1:$

When~$x < 10$

$g\left(x\right) = 15 - \left|10 - x - 5\right|$

$⇒ g ( x ) = 15 - \left|5 - x\right|$

Now if~$x < 5$,~then~$g\left(x\right) = 15 - 5 + x = x + 10$

And if~$x \ge 5$,~then~$g ( x ) = 15 + 5 - x = 20 - x$

Case~$2:$~$x \ge 10$

$g\left(x\right) = 15 - \left|x - 10 - 5\right|$

$⇒ g ( x ) = 15 - \left|x - 15\right|$

Now if~$10 \le x < 15$

$⇒ g\left(x\right) = 15 - 15 + x$

So,~$g\left(x\right) = x$

Now for~$x \ge 15$, then~$g\left(x\right) = 15 - x + 15 = 30 - x$

~
$g\left(x\right) = \left\{$\begin{cases}x + 10, & x < 5 \\ 20 - x, & 5 \le x < 10 \\ x, & 10 < x \le 15 \\ 30 - x, & x \ge 15\end{cases}$\right$

Now, it is clear from the graph of~$g \left(x\right)$~has sharp corners at$x = 5, 10, 15$~and hence this function is not differentiable at~$x = 5, 10, 15 .$

$$

So~$16 + 4b = {∫}_{0}^{3}\left($2 - t\right)dt + {∫}_{3}^{4}\left($8 - t\right)dt$

$⇒ 16 + 4b = {2t - $\dfrac{t2}{2}}_{0}^{3} + {8t - $\dfrac{t2}{2}}_{3}^{4}$

$⇒ 16 + 4b = 15$

So~$b = $\dfrac{- 1}{4}

Now differentiating~$f \left(x\right)$~we get,

$f^{'}\left(x\right) = \left\{$\begin{cases}\left(5 - \left|x - 3\right|\right), & x > 4 \\ 2x + b, & x < 4\end{cases}$\right$

Now at~$x = 4$

$LHD = 2x + b = 2 \times 4 - \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{31}{4}$

$LHD \ne RHD$

And~$f^{'} \left($3\right) + f^{'} \left(5\right) = \dfrac{23}{4} +3 = \dfrac{35}{4}$

So, option~\left(B\right)$~is true

Now~$f\left(x\right) = x^{2} - \dfrac{x}{4}$~at~$x ≤ 4$

$f^{'}\left(x\right) = 2x - \dfrac{1}{4}$

Thus the function is not increasing in the interval in~$x \in \left(- \infty , \dfrac{1}{8}\right)$

So, option~ \left(C\right)$~is NOT TRUE.

And function~$f \left($x\right)$~is also have local minima at~$x = $\dfrac{1}{8}~so option~ \left(D\right)$ \text{ and } is also true.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
f: [ 0, \infty ) \to [ 0, \infty )$,~$f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}\left[y\right]dy$

Let $x = n + f, f \in ( 0, 1 )$

$⇒ \left[x\right] = n, \left\{x\right\} = f$.

So
